Senior R Package Developer

Description

Join a team building critical infrastructure for genomics research. You'll own and evolve a multi-package R ecosystem that enables scientists worldwide to perform reproducible, scalable bioinformatics analysis. Your work directly impacts scientific discovery—when your code runs reliably, researchers can focus on science instead of infrastructure.

This role combines deep technical challenges (coordinating releases across 20+ interdependent packages, optimizing cloud storage integration, maintaining Bioconductor compatibility) with meaningful autonomy. You'll balance modernization with stability, make architectural decisions independently, and become the expert others rely on. If you value craft, depth, and sustained impact over constantly chasing new projects, this role offers a rare opportunity for mastery.

Technical Portfolio

Platform Infrastructure

Client-side caching systems with integrity verification
Version management and environment configuration

Data Access Layer
REST API clients with complex upload/download logic and cloud storage integration
Data management packages with lazy loading and provenance tracking
Compatibility layers for evolving backend systems

Object Serialization
Multi-package framework for schema-driven serialization to portable formats
Performance-critical components with compiled code
Support for diverse Bioconductor data structures across genomics workflows

Responsibilities

Core Engineering (60%)
Coordinate releases across interdependent R packages in sync with Bioconductor's biannual cycle
Maintain backward compatibility while modernizing codebases
Resolve bugs, security issues, and user-reported problems
Ensure comprehensive test coverage and CI/CD health

Strategic Modernization (20%)
Refactor legacy systems toward current best practices
Reduce technical debt in authentication, caching, and upload systems
Improve documentation, testing, and developer experience

Collaboration & Integration (20%)
Ensure compatibility with evolving backend APIs and infrastructure
Support downstream developers building on these packages
Coordinate with infrastructure and data engineering teams

Requirements
Must Have
3+ years developing production R packages
Strong understanding of S4 object system and generic method dispatch
Experience with Bioconductor ecosystem and release cycles
Proficiency with modern R development tools (`testthat`, `roxygen2`, CI/CD)
REST API integration and authentication patterns (OAuth2, JWT)
Track record of maintaining production systems and managing technical debt

Preferred
Cloud object storage integration (multipart uploads, presigned URLs, temporary credentials)
File formats: HDF5, CSV, JSON Schema validation
Database systems (SQLite, distributed search)
C++/Rcpp for performance-critical code
Bioinformatics domain knowledge (genomic data structures, workflows)
Open-source contributions demonstrating sustained project involvement

Why This Role
Deep Technical Challenges: Master the intersection of R, Bioconductor, cloud infrastructure, authentication, and distributed systems. Solve complex dependency graphs, optimize performance-critical paths, and design for reliability at scale.

Direct Scientific Impact: Your code enables genomics research worldwide. When your packages work seamlessly, researchers can focus on discovery instead of infrastructure problems.

Ownership & Autonomy: Make architectural decisions, set priorities, and drive technical direction. You'll be the recognized expert others depend on.

Sustainable Pace: Remote-friendly, async collaboration. Focus on quality over speed. Build systems that last years, not months.

Work Environment
Location: Remote (US/Europe time zones preferred)
Team: You'll work independently most days, with regular collaboration across backend engineers, infrastructure teams, and data scientists
Tools: Git/GitLab, R/RStudio, Linux/macOS, CI/CD pipelines
Culture Fit: You'll thrive if you enjoy solving complex puzzles, value quality over speed, and find satisfaction in systems that work reliably year after year
